Version: 6.3.1

API name: get information of an interface
Parameter_fabricName: Network1

Parameter_podId: 10

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

message.content:
Below is the exact REST‑ful GET request you would send to the Cisco Nexus Dashboard (v6.3.1) to retrieve the **Speed** information for an Ethernet interface on node 12 in pod 10 of fabric “Network1”.

---

### 1. URL & Query Parameters

```
GET https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo
    ?fabricName=Network1
    &nodeId=12
    &podId=10
    &interfaceType=Ethernet
    &infoType=Speed
```

> **Endpoint**  
> `https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo`  
> (replace `{ip}` with your device’s IP)

> **Query parameters**  
> * `fabricName` – name of the fabric (e.g., `Network1`)  
> * `nodeId` – numeric ID of the node (e.g., `12`)  
> * `podId` – numeric ID of the pod (e.g., `10`)  
> * `interfaceType` – type of interface (`Ethernet`, `gigabitethernet`, etc.)  
> * `infoType` – type of information requested (`Speed`, `statistics`, etc.)

---

### 2. cURL Example

```bash
curl -X GET \
  "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=Ethernet&infoType=Speed" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_TOKEN>"
```

> **Note** – Replace `<YOUR_TOKEN>` with the bearer token or basic auth credentials that your Nexus Dashboard requires.

---

### 3. Python (using the provided `requests_get` helper)

```python
from functions import requests_get

response = requests_get({
    "url": "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo",
    "params": {
        "fabricName": "Network1",
        "nodeId": 12,
        "podId": 10,
        "interfaceType": "Ethernet",
        "infoType": "Speed"
    }
})

print(response.json())
```

---

### 4. What to Expect

The response will be a JSON payload containing the speed (in Mbps or Gbps) of the specified Ethernet interface, along with any other metadata the API returns for that query.

---

#### Quick Checklist

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Base URL | `https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo` |
| fabricName | `Network1` |
| nodeId | `12` |
| podId | `10` |
| interfaceType | `Ethernet` |
| infoType | `Speed` |
| Auth | Bearer token / Basic Auth (as required) |

That’s all you need to generate and execute the RESTful request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard. Happy querying!
